name: party-state-counterfactual
symbols_from_why: Runs against the PINNED BASE ROM: every symbol it reads is vanilla.
description: The third counterfactual for party-state, and the only one that is orthogonal to BOTH of the others. --counterfactual moves the addresses; --no-savestate changes the memory contents; this spec changes neither -- it reads exactly the right bytes out of exactly the right save state and expects the WRONG values. It is the one that proves the assertions in party-state.json are load-bearing rather than tautological: run it with --expect-fail and it must exit 0.

assert.why: WRONG BY ONE. The lead is level 5. An off-by-one is the failure a level-cap or EXP-curve hack would actually produce, so this is the shape of error the harness has to be able to see.
WRONG BY ONE. Current HP is 20. Same argument: a damage-formula change moves HP by small amounts, not by orders of magnitude.
WRONG. The player owns one Pokemon, not two.
WRONG. The deref reaches map 1.4 (Birch's lab), not 1.9. Proves the pointer chase is reading the map and not just any readable byte.
WRONG SYMBOL. gSaveBlock1Ptr resolves into gSaveblock1; naming the other saveblock must fail. This is the check that would catch a probe wired to the wrong pointer.
WRONG SCREEN. The state resumes into CB2_Overworld; expecting the intro callback is what a spec would look like if it had silently failed to load the save state at all.
WRONG OUTCOME. B_OUTCOME_LOST where the engine holds B_OUTCOME_WON. This is the assertion shape a difficulty hack's verification will live or die on, so it had better be able to fail.
